silver nanoparticles were biosynthesized using Zizyphi spinosae L aqueous leaves extracts and the biosynthesized silver nano particles were characterized by UV-vis, FTIR, TEM and XRD techniques.
ZSE was able to form AgNPs at room temperature in a short period of time and the green synthesized nanoparticles exhibited significant antibacterial properties.
the Zizyphu s spina christi leaf extract has the potential to synthesize silver nanoparticle in few minutes at room temperature.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biosynthesis and characterization of silver nanoparticles using aqueous leaf extract of Z. spina christi and their therapeutic application.
the synthesis of AgNPs from ZSE and the evaluation of their antibacterial activity.
the synthesis, characterization and evaluation of antibacterial efficacy of green synthesized silver nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present study has successfully demonstrated the synthesis of silver nanoparticles using ZSE, and their antibacterial efficacy in therapeutic application.
the green synthesis method of silver nanoparticles using ZSE is a simple and rapid technique for the synthesis of nanoparticles.
the biosynthesized silver nanoparticle using ZSE has a potential for therapeutic application in wound dressing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the biosynthesized Ag nanoparticles could be a potential antibacterial agent for treating wounds and preventing wound infections.
the biosynthesised silver nanoparticles were effective against the tested bacteria, thus, they can be used as an effective antibacterial agent in wound dressing and other medical applications.
ZSE has the potential to form nanoparticles within few minutes and the nanoparticles could be used to treat multi drug resistant bacteria.

the silver nanoparticles can be prepared in an ecofriendly and cost-effective method, and they have potential for antibacterial activity.
the silver nanoparticles synthesized by Zizyphu s spina-christi leaf extract can be used as an alternative to antibiotics in the treatment of wound infections and other infections.
